domain: A teaching hospital's double bind between training the next generation of surgeons on real patients and guaranteeing every patient the most experienced hands available
topic: A teaching hospital's double bind between training the next generation of surgeons on real patients and guaranteeing every patient the most experienced hands available

movement.gist: Stage the patient's-claim side: a patient wheeled into surgery has a right to expect the steadiest, most practiced hands in the building; define 'informed consent' as disclosure of who exactly will hold the scalpel and how many times they've held it before.

Stage the profession's-claim side: every attending was once a trembling resident who had to make a first incision on a living person; without real patients as training ground, expertise cannot be replenished and future patients inherit a hollowed-out profession.

Refuse to let either side win outright — teaching hospitals cannot honor both maximal present competence and future competence-production at once, and no reform (simulation labs, staged supervision) fully closes the gap; this is not a communication failure but a structural one.

Reread paragraph 1's seemingly neutral definition of 'informed consent' and show it already smuggled a verdict: defining consent as disclosure of the operator's identity quietly treats the patient as sole stakeholder in a room that always contains at least two futures being paid for.

Tally who actually pays: patients at teaching hospitals absorb a diffuse, statistically real but individually invisible risk; residents absorb the shame and fear of learning in public on bodies that can't consent to being practice; the institution absorbs neither cost, only the credit for both outcomes.

primary.axis: who the operating table is ultimately for
poles: the patient's claim to the most skilled hands available now
the profession's need to let novices operate on real bodies to ever become skilled hands

secondary.axis: how 'informed consent' is defined at the outset
poles: consent as disclosure of a named surgeon's identity and experience
consent as disclosure that teaching hospitals are, structurally, always partly run by learners

tension_system.interaction: the secondary tension is the hinge that makes the primary one undecidable: how 'informed consent' gets defined quietly decides, in advance, who is counted as bearing the cost of training

family_realization.note: Double bind executed flawlessly: patient demands 'most practiced hand' (skill now); profession demands training ground (skill later). Passage refuses both-and; instead maps distribution: patient absorbs statistical risk, resident absorbs shame, institution absorbs neither. No side endorsed; all side-picking distractors fail structurally.

ending_behavior.note: 'Someone has to learn on someone' reopened from resignation to indictment. Truism now means: names exactly who pays (patient, resident) and who takes credit (institution). Aperture truly narrows from structural inevitability to precise cost allocation. Refusal suspended—bind remains.

voice_consistency.note: Patient Explicator throughout: generous first definition, honest repositioning in paragraph 4 ('return to that first, generous definition'), knife turns in final third. Concrete particular: 'faint tremor she had to overrule.' Uneven polish: 'Call this the patient's demand' vs. analytical density. No generic AI-essay register.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(D): half-truth trap—correct answer's _target_, not its conclusion. Q2(A): stage-misattribution—shifts system cost to individual resident. Q3(B): false partnership—passage stresses patient never consented to being practice. Q4(A): premature-closure—addresses disclosure, not structural necessity. Traps genuine, not lexical extremes.

explanation_quality.note: Every wrong answer tied to specific mechanism: scope_inflation (P3 narrows gap, never closes), causal_inversion (P5 says institution absorbs neither cost), stage_misattribution (bind is systemic, not individual), false_symmetry (risk ≠ shame). Zero lazy 'not mentioned.' Precise passage locations cited.

Financing metaphor refers to costs paid via risk/hardship by patient and resident, not literal money.
If simulation matches live training, the bind (skill now vs later requiring live patients) dissolves.
Mirrors passage's structure: institution banks credit while passengers/students bear the costs.
Text says definition 'decided who is permitted to be the sole injured party,' matching C directly.
This anecdote introduces the competing demand: skill must be grown, creating the structural bind.
